subject: general
question: Which of the following is involved in emulsification of fats?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liver**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Liver

 
 
• The liver is the largest gland in the human body.
 
• **It also secretes bile necessary for the digestion of fats (emulsification of fats).**
 
• The liver is where both glycogenolysis and glycogenesis take place.
 
• Dark/Reddish Brown, vital organ.
 
• Described as having a **double blood supply.**
 
• Lies on the** right side** of the **abdominal cavity beneath the diaphragm.**
 
• In males, it weighs from** 1.4 to 1.6 kilograms,** in females from **1.2 to 1.4 kilograms.**
 
• The Liver is extremely resilient and capable of regenerating itself.
 
 
 
• Functions:
 
 
• Production of bile that helps in digestion in the small intestine.
 
• Production of cholesterol and special proteins that helps carry fats in the body.
 
• Converts excess glucose to glycogen. Glycogen is later stored in the liver.
 
• Regulates the level of amino acids in the blood.
 
• Helps in clearing the blood of toxins.
 
• Regulates blood clotting.
 
• **Helps in clearing bilirubin from the body.**
